channel.title: Arble Blog
channel.description: Engineering, research and product writing from Arble.

item.title: Memory beyond the context window
item.description: A context window is working memory, not storage. What retrieval looks like when the unit is a fact with provenance rather than a chunk of text.

item.title: Typing 579 tools without slowing the loop
item.description: Registry lookup was 400 ms at the ninety-ninth percentile once workspaces passed a few hundred tools. What we changed, and why the obvious cache was the wrong fix.

item.title: Designing the permission gate
item.description: Every write stops to ask. The hard part is not the prompt — it is deciding what counts as one decision, and how to avoid training people to approve without reading.

item.title: How tool calling actually works
item.description: From JSON schema to a validated call and back into the transcript, including the failure modes that only appear once a model can call forty things.

item.title: The architecture behind sessions
item.description: What a session owns, what it borrows, and how compaction preserves the instructions that set it up rather than the small talk that followed.

item.title: Introducing the Tool SDK
item.description: Decorators, generated schemas, streaming results and publishing, in four languages. Why the SDK generates the schema instead of asking you to write it.

item.title: Coordinating agents without a queue
item.description: Multi-agent work looks like a distributed system because it is one. What we borrowed from actor models, and where the analogy breaks.

item.title: Why local-first matters for agents
item.description: Latency is the smaller argument. The larger one is that an agent holding your keys and your context is a different trust proposition to one holding a copy.

item.title: MCP versus native tools
item.description: When to write a tool into the runtime and when to reach for a protocol server, measured on latency, typing, failure handling and who you are trusting.

item.title: Observability for systems that decide
item.description: A trace that stops at the HTTP boundary tells you nothing about why an agent chose a tool. Instrumenting the loop itself.

item.title: Building desktop automation on an untrusted network
item.description: Pairing, key exchange and the relay that carries ciphertext it cannot read. Plus the host-key problem we have not solved yet.

item.title: Planning versus reasoning
item.description: Two words used interchangeably that describe different mechanisms with different failure modes. Why conflating them produces agents that think beautifully and do nothing.

item.title: Running Arble on Kubernetes
item.description: Readiness against liveness, draining a node mid-run, and why additive migrations are what make a rolling upgrade possible at all.

item.title: Inside the CLI
item.description: Designing a command surface that is pleasant to type and safe to script — including why every command has a --json mode.

item.title: Streaming responses, and what breaks at the edges
item.description: Token boundaries, backpressure, and the disconnect bug that silently discarded work for two releases before we understood it.
